Fit a two-level latent class model: classes of categorical responses and classes of the groups they are nested in

Source: R/multilca.R
multilca.Rd

multilca() fits a latent class model for categorical data with observations nested within groups. It describes response patterns through latent classes and differences between groups through the relative prevalence of those classes. Groups with similar class compositions are represented by the same latent group class.

By default, the response probabilities defining the observation-level classes are shared across groups. The model estimates these probabilities together with class proportions and posterior membership probabilities, allowing both observations and groups to be classified while retaining information about classification uncertainty.

Usage

multilca(data, vars, id, n_profiles, n_group_classes = 2L, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation.

vars

Names of the indicator columns. Numeric, integer, logical, character and factor columns are accepted, and every distinct value of a column is one category; factor levels retain their declared order and other types are sorted.

id

Name of the group identifier column, or NULL for a single-level model (lca() fits that directly).

n_profiles

Number of observation-level latent classes (profiles).

n_group_classes

Number of group-level latent classes. Defaults to 2, or to 1 when id = NULL. With 1, the groups do not differ in their class proportions.

...

Further arguments, passed to multilpa(), which documents all of them. The ones used most often:

  • missing: "error" (default) stops when an indicator has a missing value; "fiml" keeps every row and uses the responses it has.

  • ordinal, count: indicators in vars modelled as ordered categories or as counts; the remaining indicators are categorical.

  • n_starts (default 10), seed, max_iter and tol: the number of starts, the seed that makes them reproducible, and the limits of each start.

  • min_probability: the lower bound on a response probability (default 1e-10).

  • profile_covariates, group_covariates: covariates that predict class and group-class membership.

  • time: the occasion column, used to order each group's rows in the sequence tables and plot_sequences().

categorical is accepted but has no further effect; its names must be in vars.

Value

A fitted model of class multilpa, or multilpa_covariates when membership covariates are specified, as returned by multilpa(). The classes are numbered 1, 2, and so on in the profile column of its tables, and the group classes in group_class. get_results() returns the tables by name, among them:

  • "responses" (also as.data.frame(fit)): one row per class, item and category, with the response probability;

  • "profile_probabilities": the proportion of each class within each group class, and the proportion of each group class;

  • "assignments": the data with each row's most likely class, its group's most likely group class and the posterior probabilities;

  • "group_posteriors": the posterior probability of each group class for each group;

  • "classification" and "entropy": how clearly rows and groups are classified;

  • "information_criteria" and "starts".

Details

The function calls multilpa(), treating all indicators in vars as categorical except those specified through ordinal or count in .... Categorical indicators have unrestricted class-specific response probabilities; ordinal and count indicators use the corresponding structured measurement models. For a combination of continuous and categorical indicators, use multilpa() with categorical.

Conditions

Errors: latents_bad_argument when id is left out or an argument has a value that is not accepted; latents_bad_categorical when categorical names a column not in vars; latents_bad_data when a column is missing from data or an indicator has missing values under missing = "error"; latents_unidentified when more than one group class is requested with one class or with one row per group. Warnings: latents_unconverged when the reported start did not converge and latents_small_classes when a class or group class is nearly empty. Otherwise the conditions of multilpa(); latents-conditions lists them all.

See also

multilpa() for continuous and mixed indicators, and vignette("lca", package = "latents").

Examples

activities <- c("time_with_friends", "on_social_media", "tv_video_games")
fit <- multilca(subset(student_esm, day <= 1), vars = activities,
                id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,
                n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
get_results(fit, "responses")
#>    profile         indicator category probability  threshold
#> 1        1 time_with_friends       no 0.975634724  3.6899293
#> 2        2 time_with_friends       no 0.829730459  1.5837182

#> 4        2 time_with_friends      yes 0.170269541         NA
